name: xtool
cost: Free to download. The API key login needs a paid Apple Developer Program membership; the password login works with any Apple ID
works_with: Linux, Windows through WSL, and macOS, with an iOS device over USB
short: Builds a Swift package into an iOS app, then signs it and installs it on your device from Linux, Windows or a Mac without Xcode's build system.
what: xtool is a command line tool that does Xcode's jobs with open standards. It builds a SwiftPM package into an iOS app, signs it, installs it on a connected device and talks to Apple Developer Services. It also comes with a Swift library, XKit, for doing the same things from your own app.
who: iOS developers who want to work on Linux or Windows, or who prefer SwiftPM and their own editor to the Xcode build system. You still need Apple's SDK: on Linux it comes from an Xcode download, and on a Mac Xcode has to be installed. If you're happy in Xcode, you can skip it.
needs: Linux and WSL: the Swift 6.4 toolchain from swift.org
Linux and WSL: usbmuxd, so xtool can talk to your device
Linux and WSL: Xcode 27 as `Xcode.xip`, downloaded in your browser with your Apple ID
Windows: WSL, plus USB passthrough set up with USBIPD
macOS: Xcode installed and launched once
An Apple ID, or an App Store Connect API key if you have a paid developer membership
An iOS device connected by USB

steps.title: Check Swift (Linux and WSL)
steps.text: Install the Swift 6.4 toolchain for your distribution from swift.org, then confirm it's there.

steps.title: Install usbmuxd if it's missing
steps.text: Run `usbmuxd --help` to check. If you get "command not found" on Ubuntu or Debian, install it:

steps.title: Download xtool (Linux and WSL)
steps.text: This fetches the latest AppImage for your architecture and puts it on your PATH. Run `xtool --help` afterwards to check.
steps.code:
curl -fL \
  "https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/releases/latest/download/xtool-$(uname -m).AppImage" \
  -o xtool
chmod +x xtool
sudo mv xtool /usr/local/bin/

steps.title: Or install it on a Mac
steps.text: With Homebrew. Without it, download `xtool.app` from the latest GitHub release, move it to Applications, launch it and run the script it suggests.

steps.title: Log in
steps.text: Pick API Key if you have a paid Apple Developer Program membership, or Password, which works with any Apple ID. On Linux it then asks for the path to `Xcode.xip` and builds an iOS Swift SDK from it.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `xtool new` to create an xtool SwiftPM project, then `xtool dev` to build and run it. The first-app tutorial on xtool.sh walks you through it.

watch: Password login uses private Apple APIs. The docs suggest a throwaway Apple ID if you want to be extra careful.
The docs say your credentials are sent only to Apple, and you can build xtool from source to check.
The Linux install uses sudo to move a downloaded file into `/usr/local/bin`.
Downloading Xcode means logging in with your Apple ID and accepting Apple's licence in the browser.
A manual Mac install doesn't update itself. Check GitHub releases yourself, or install with Homebrew.
On WSL, if you hit `AFCClient.Error.muxError`, the docs link an issue comment that relays the device through iTunes on Windows instead.
